_comment: How each source spells our minerals. Sources that carry facility or production rows
name commodities in prose rather than in HS codes, and they do not agree with each
other: ICMM records rare earths as 'lanthanides', 'REE', 'monazite' or the name of a
single element, while the IEA calls the same group 'Magnet rare earth elements'.
Tokens are matched case-insensitively against whole comma-, semicolon- or
slash-separated fragments of a source field, so 'ree' does not match 'greener'. The
mineral's own name from minerals.json is always matched too and does not need repeating
here. Adding a fifth mineral means adding a key here, not editing a source module.
Note that ICMM's rare-earth coverage is thin: a handful of sites carry a rare-earth
token at all, because the dataset is built around large-scale operations reported by
ICMM members and most separation capacity is not.
